review.title: Coculture Faecalibacterium descriptor: scoped M5 ambiguity diagnostic
review.independence_basis: Authored source and database assessment. Parent independently inspected the source plan, actual source anchors, native alternatives, unchanged partner block and local candidate; then independently verified the M5 candidate and receipt before application. A peer separately reviewed the shared source binder and its actual-consumer locator regression. This saved assessment remains authored, not an independent full scientific approval.
review.summary: The existing Faecalibacterium prausnitzii species descriptor has three native alternatives in the exact pinned crosswalk. The guarded M5 correction records AMBIGUOUS and all three alternatives without selecting a GTDB identity for study stock A2-165/JCM31915. B. bifidum's existing classification, both study stocks, all biological claims and prior history remain unchanged. Actual application, native append-only history and eight required commands are bound.
review.scope_description: The taxonomy[1] GTDB status and complete alternatives, source/stock boundary, actual application and scoped native checks. This is not a new whole-record scientific review.
review.selection: One whole record, CommunityMech:000401, chosen as the first status-only unit through the shared engine after its accepted species-reference canary and the completed separate 000546 ambiguity canary. No wider status-only batch precedes this saved unit.
limitations: Partial technical/provenance assessment with scientific_review:false; no full scientific approval, corpus QC pass, or release clearance.

The alternatives belong to the current stored NCBI species descriptor, not an independently verified assembly classification of A2-165. Primary Methods uses F. prausnitzii, while a cited 2024 title uses F. duncaniae; that strain-level nomenclature question remains outside this bounded correction.
The complete candidate set is preserved in native order. No exact-stock identity, support-genome denominator, candidate probability or majority is inferred from an ambiguous route.

Local and M5 source binders retain separate database file-stat observations. Their label/rank rows agree, but neither the complete NCBI database content nor its release is certified by a whole-database checksum. The crosswalk, source cache, XML, native resolver and all captured assessment files have exact hashes.

The existing 472-genome B. bifidum block remains byte-for-byte unchanged, including its historical mapping-source wording. This status-only assessment does not independently re-certify that block's release/build claim or exact study-stock placement.

The open bifido_faecali_2fl_fos_flux_unresolved discussion remains unchanged. Donor-resolved acetate flux, pH and residual-substrate limitations, functional roles and other whole-record scientific questions are not cleared here.

Seven scoped native validators and native history scaffolding passed. Reference-snippet matching, generated pages, strict historical successor integration and final combined full QC are separately accounted work. Required passing native checks do not make this a full scientific review.

evidence.locator: Methods2.1; retained cache character1763/line12, Discussion character6818/line32; independently retained PMC13515949 XML
evidence.summary: Methods identifies A2-165/JCM31915 and B. bifidum JCM1254. The Discussion explicitly says metabolic flux was not directly measured. This supports preserving the reported stocks and inference limits; it does not select an exact-stock GTDB species.

Exact pinned native species-name resolution of NCBITaxon:853 yields F. longum, F. prausnitzii and F. prausnitzii_D. The current M5 NCBI label/rank agrees with the captured descriptor; all alternatives remain explicit with no stock placement or population denominator inferred.

Actual guarded M5 replacement persisted the independently accepted candidate: one status, three candidate identifiers and one native inline event. All other canonical science and previous history remain exact. The native sidecar and all eight current command receipts are separately hash-bound.

Historical scientific decisions and later abundance remediation remain unchanged. The two graph nodes distinguish an observed ratio-dependent butyrate peak from inferred donor transfer; this diagnostic does not replace those judgments or resolve the open pH/substrate/flux discussion.

assessments.summary: Retain source A2-165/JCM31915 naming and canonical NCBITaxon:853. The complete database alternative set does not establish the study strain's species cluster or settle the cited F. duncaniae nomenclature context.
